summary: Use module-runtime fallback for top-level await because it changes asynchronous ECMAScript module evaluation and dependency ordering.

target.notes: Preserve async module execution, dependency waiting, rejection propagation, and module-graph cycle behavior.

semantics.graph: ordering depends on module dependency graph

caveats: C# top-level await in an entry point is not equivalent to ECMAScript module-graph evaluation.

tests.name: dependent module waits
tests.input: // a.mjs: await Promise.resolve(); export const x=1; // b.mjs: import {x} from './a.mjs'; console.log(x);
tests.expected_behavior: b executes only after a finishes asynchronous module evaluation

tests.name: top-level rejection fails module
tests.expected_behavior: module evaluation fails with rejection reason x under the selected module host
